heading: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - SUBBASEMENT ARCHIVE - DAY

units.text: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - SUBBASEMENT ARCHIVE - DAY
Steel shelves in ranks, boxed files stacked to the ceiling, a bare bulb on a cord.
The air smells of paper rot and lemon oil.
At the end of one aisle, a folding table has been set for a deposition.
COUNSEL ELIAS PRESCOTT, 50s, in a rumpled navy suit, sits with a legal pad and a pen he clicks nervously.
SALMA RAHIMI-DUBOIS, 30s, a court reporter, hunches over a steno machine, fingers poised.
EULALIE FONTAINE, 70s, the witness, in a lace collar and sensible shoes, sits across the table with a handbag in her lap and a face like a closed book.
Mrs. Fontaine, please state your name for the record.
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Eulalie Marguerite Fontaine.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: And you were employed as the archivist here from 1988 to 2019?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Thirty-one years.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: During that time, you maintained the records of all property transfers in this county.
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: I maintained them. I did not alter them.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: No one has said you did.
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: You are about to.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: Prescott's pen stops clicking.
Salma's fingers flit across the keys, catching every word.
Mrs. Fontaine, I'm handing you Exhibit F. Do you recognize it?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: It is a deed.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: For which parcel?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Lot 14, Mill Street.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: Whose signature is that?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Hmm. It appears to be Mr. Aldous Quinn's.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: And do you see a notary seal?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: I do.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: Whose?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Mine.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: A beat.
The bulb sways.
Dust floats down through its glow.
Did you notarize this document, ma'am?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: I did not.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: But it bears your seal.
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: It does.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: Then who stamped it?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Someone with a key to my drawer.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: Salma stops typing.
Looks up.
Eulalie meets her gaze, then turns back to Prescott.
Mr. Prescott. I have kept that drawer locked for thirty-one years. I have given one key to one person. I have never regretted it until this morning.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: Who has the key, Mrs. Fontaine?
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: Your client.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: The pen drops.
Prescott does not pick it up.
His face is white.
Salma's fingers resume, steadier now, taking down every syllable.
Madam reporter, strike that.
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: I can't strike it. It's on the record.
units.name: SALMA

units.text: Strike it.
units.name: PRESCOTT

units.text: No, sir.
units.name: SALMA

units.text: Eulalie opens her handbag.
Takes out a ring of keys.
Sets it gently on the table, with a small clink that echoes through the stacks.
There are two. Mine, and his.
units.name: EULALIE

units.text: She slides the ring toward Prescott.
He stares at it.
Overhead, the bulb flickers.
The archive hums.
